## Contract

The agreement a customer is billed under. `title`, `contractNumber`, `contractType`, the linked CRM `account` and `deal` (an Opportunity), an HR Employee `owner`, `status` (Contract Status: draft → negotiating → in review → approved → out for signature → signed, plus expired and terminated, with an explicit transition map), `value` (base `AmountWithCurrency`), markdown `terms`, and an approval chain.

```ts
import { Contract } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/legal/contract';

@field contract = linksTo(() => Contract);
```

### Parties and the signature ceremony

`parties` (Legal Party Role) says who is bound and in what capacity. `signatureBlocks` (Signature Block) is the signature page: one line per signer in signing order, our side linked to a Signatory whose authority is checked. Request Signature, Verify Signature and Execute Contract (`cards/legal/commands/`) drive it: request one line at a time, verify order and authority, and move to `signed` only when every line is signed; the Signature Block View renders it.

### Term and the notice deadline

`effectivePeriod` (the Effective Period field) holds the term; `noticeBy` is the date notice must be served to stop an auto-renewal and `daysToNotice` counts down to it, because the expiry is common knowledge and the notice deadline is the date that quietly passes. `startDate`, `endDate`, `autoRenews` and `renewalNoticeDays` are the flat form of the same facts; when an Effective Period is set it is the one that is read.

### Clauses and obligations

Contract Clause and Obligation each link **up** to their contract, and the contract's isolated view reads them back with a query on that link. There are deliberately no `clauses` or `obligations` arrays here: obligations are unbounded, and a back-link would put Contract in an import cycle with both modules.

### Signing and the document

`signedAt` is written once and `isSigned` computes from it, so a signature survives a later status change. `daysToExpiry` reads 0 for a terminated agreement, so a renewal view sorts by urgency without a stored countdown. The executed copy is referenced (`documentUrl`, `executedCopyUrl`), not held.

### Examples

`Contract/acme-msa-2026` is signed, with its clauses and obligations; `Contract/acme-expansion-order-form` is out for signature with line 1 signed and line 2 requested; `Contract/acme-co-marketing` has a declined line and a signatory over their ceiling; `Contract/brightleaf-pilot-terms` and `Contract/nadia-lapsed` have no signature page.

**Non-goals:** generating the document text, a live e-signature integration (the commands record the provider's reference), and renewal automation.
